content.title: Subway Collision Fight | Environment Impact, Recovery, Grounded Counter
content.summary: A station mechanic recovers from a timetable-wall collision and repels a saboteur. Preserve the five causal invariants, stable spatial anchors and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: One fixed environment anchor proves the initial impact. + Recovery occurs in the same damaged location. + The opponent enters along an established axis. + Every counter has grounded visible contact. + The final direct action follows a resolved spatial exchange.
quick_start.recommended_input: Throw one adult station mechanic against a fixed glass timetable wall and show one localized crack. Bring one adult saboteur down the established platform lane into close range. Finish with the mechanic driving one gloved palm toward camera as the saboteur exits the lane.
required_anchors: One fixed environment anchor proves the initial impact.
Recovery occurs in the same damaged location.
Every counter has grounded visible contact.
The final direct action follows a resolved spatial exchange.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: A station mechanic recovers from a timetable-wall collision and repels a saboteur. Preserve the five causal invariants, stable spatial anchors and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.
